data.title: Shareholders Can Be Confident That Capital Asset Planning's (TSE:3965) Earnings Are High Quality
data.description:
Capital Asset Planning, Inc.'s (TSE:3965) strong earnings report was rewarded with a positive stock price move. We have done some analysis, and we found several positive factors beyond the profit numbers.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

A Closer Look At Capital Asset Planning's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Capital Asset Planning recorded an accrual ratio of -0.53. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. In fact, it had free cash flow of JP¥2.1b in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of JP¥602.0m. Capital Asset Planning's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Capital Asset Planning.

Our Take On Capital Asset Planning's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, Capital Asset Planning produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Because of this, we think Capital Asset Planning's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! Better yet, its EPS are growing strongly, which is nice to see. At the end of the day, it's essential to consider more than just the factors above, if you want to understand the company properly. If you'd like to know more about Capital Asset Planning as a business, it's important to be aware of any risks it's facing. At Simply Wall St, we found 2 warning signs for Capital Asset Planning and we think they deserve your attention.

data.title: Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad Just Missed Earnings - But Analysts Have Updated Their Models
data.description:
The analysts might have been a bit too bullish on Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad (KLSE:MRDIY), given that the company fell short of expectations when it released its third-quarter results last week. It wasn't a great result overall - while revenue fell marginally short of analyst estimates at RM1.3b, statutory earnings missed forecasts by an incredible 29%, coming in at just RM0.013 per share. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the current consensus from Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad's 16 analysts is for revenues of RM5.55b in 2027. This would reflect an okay 7.3% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to rise 6.0% to RM0.069. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of RM5.71b and earnings per share (EPS) of RM0.075 in 2027. The analysts are less bullish than they were before these results, given the reduced revenue forecasts and the small dip in earnings per share expectations.

Check out our latest analysis for Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad

It'll come as no surprise then, to learn that the analysts have cut their price target 26% to RM1.33. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. There are some variant perceptions on Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at RM2.15 and the most bearish at RM0.81 per share. With such a wide range in price targets, analysts are almost certainly betting on widely divergent outcomes in the underlying business. With this in mind, we wouldn't rely too heavily the consensus price target, as it is just an average and analysts clearly have some deeply divergent views on the business.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. We would highlight that Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad's revenue growth is expected to slow, with the forecast 5.8% annualised growth rate until the end of 2027 being well below the historical 8.6% p.a. growth over the last five years. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 1.5% annually. So it's pretty clear that, while Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad's revenue growth is expected to slow, it's still expected to grow faster than the industry itself.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that the analysts downgraded their earnings per share estimates, showing that there has been a clear decline in sentiment following these results. Regrettably, they also downgraded their revenue estimates, but the latest forecasts still imply the business will grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad's future valuation.

With that said, the long-term trajectory of the company's earnings is a lot more important than next year. We have estimates - from multiple Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad analysts - going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

It is also worth noting that we have found 1 warning sign for Mr D.I.Y. Group (M) Berhad that you need to take into consideration.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Importantly, our data indicates that TOMATOSYSTEMLtd's profit received a boost of ₩988m in unusual items, over the last year. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. TOMATOSYSTEMLtd had a rather significant contribution from unusual items relative to its profit to September 2026. An Unusual Tax Situation

Just as we noted the unusual items, we must inform you that TOMATOSYSTEMLtd received a tax benefit which contributed ₩865m to the bottom line. This is of course a bit out of the ordinary, given it is more common for companies to be paying tax than receiving tax benefits! We're sure the company was pleased with its tax benefit. And given that it lost money last year, it seems possible that the benefit is evidence that it now expects to find value in its past tax losses. However, our data indicates that tax benefits can temporarily boost statutory profit in the year it is booked, but subsequently profit may fall back. Assuming the tax benefit is not repeated every year, we could see its profitability drop noticeably, all else being equal. So while we think it's great to receive a tax benefit, it does tend to imply an increased risk that the statutory profit overstates the sustainable earnings power of the business.

Our Take On TOMATOSYSTEMLtd's Profit Performance

In its last report TOMATOSYSTEMLtd received a tax benefit which might make its profit look better than it really is on a underlying level. Furthermore, it also benefitted from a positive unusual item, which boosted the profit result even higher. On reflection, the above-mentioned factors give us the strong impression that TOMATOSYSTEMLtd'sunderlying earnings power is not as good as it might seem, based on the statutory profit numbers. data.title: Everpure (EVRP) Stock Climbs As Q3 Results Back Margin Strength
data.description:
Everpure entered this Q3 2027 report with a punchy story on paper: high earnings growth, a rich P/E of 117.6x, and a share price that had fallen 16.6% over the past month. Then the quarter hit. Revenue reached US$1.46b and net income came in at US$100.4m, and the stock jumped 4.7% to US$105.46 in Thursday trading.

The reaction looks like relief mixed with renewed conviction. A business priced for perfection is now trying to prove that its margin strength and cash generation can support that kind of valuation.

Love Everpure’s margin story but uneasy about paying a 117.6x P/E for it? Compare this quarter with a curated 34 high quality undervalued stocks to see what stronger value-for-money combinations look like.

Q3 2027 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$1,459.8m vs. US$964.5m (up 51%)
  • Net Income, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$100.4m vs. US$54.8m (up 83%)
  • Basic EPS, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$0.30 vs. US$0.17 (up 81%)
  • Total Gross Margin, Q3 2027: 69.2% (product gross margin 67.3%, subscription gross margin 72.6%)

Everpure says recent hyperscale deals carry 75–85% gross margins. Ask Charlie what makes Everpure’s hyperscale margins so rich.

Everpure’s Bull Story Meets Hyperscale Reality

The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St hangs a lot on Everpure turning hyperscale wins and software into a step change in profitability.

"Hyperscale DirectFlash design wins with two top 5 cloud providers, combined with expected hyperscale shipments at 75% to 85% product gross margins and committed orders that extend through at least 2028, create potential for a re rating of Everpure's margin profile if this OEM like stream becomes a larger share of total product revenue and lifts overall gross margin."

Q3 goes a fair way toward that milestone. Product gross margin of 67.3% sat inside the 65% to 70% long term range while total gross margin reached 69.2%, with management explicitly linking part of that uplift to higher margin hyperscale deployments. Subscription still carries the richer 72.6% margin, yet hyperscale Solutions materially increased its contribution and helped deliver a record 24% operating margin alongside raised full year guidance.

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for.

Everpure Bear Case: Cash Strain Fades, Contract Risk Lingers

Bearish analysts on Simply Wall St argue that Everpure’s growth engines could overreach and strain the balance between demand, contracts, and cash generation.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Evergreen//One, hyperscale DirectFlash deployments and AI data products such as Everpure Data Intelligence and Data Stream keep converting strong customer interest and contract value into durable, high margin revenue without overstraining cash flow or operating expenses."

Q3 edges against that concern. Revenue, operating income, and margins all improved while free cash flow reached US$265m and management still guides to US$600m to US$800m for FY27. The stress point now sits more in concentration risk and future usage optimization, since ARR of more than US$2.2b and remaining performance obligations above US$4.1b increase exposure if large customers slow deployments or renegotiate.

data.title: We Think Shareholders Should Be Aware Of Some Factors Beyond QD Laser's (TSE:6613) Profit
data.description:
Investors were disappointed with QD Laser, Inc.'s (TSE:6613) recent earnings release. Our analysis found several concerning factors in the earnings report beyond the strong statutory profit number.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Zooming In On QD Laser's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, QD Laser recorded an accrual ratio of 0.59. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. And indeed, during the period the company didn't produce any free cash flow whatsoever. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of JP¥1.1b, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of JP¥231.0m. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of JP¥1.1b, this year, indicates high risk. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

View our latest analysis for QD Laser

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

The fact that the company had unusual items boosting profit by JP¥413m, in the last year, probably goes some way to explain why its accrual ratio was so weak. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. When we crunched the numbers on thousands of publicly listed companies, we found that a boost from unusual items in a given year is often not repeated the next year. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. QD Laser had a rather significant contribution from unusual items relative to its profit to September 2026. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit a poor guide to underlying earnings power.

Our Take On QD Laser's Profit Performance

QD Laser had a weak accrual ratio, but its profit did receive a boost from unusual items. For all the reasons mentioned above, we think that, at a glance, QD Laser's statutory profits could be considered to be low quality, because they are likely to give investors an overly positive impression of the company. data.title: Investors Shouldn't Be Too Comfortable With KAON Group's (KOSDAQ:078890) Earnings
data.description:
Despite announcing strong earnings, KAON Group Co., Ltd.'s (KOSDAQ:078890) stock was sluggish. We did some digging and found some worrying underlying problems.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Examining Cashflow Against KAON Group's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

KAON Group has an accrual ratio of 0.31 for the year to September 2026. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit, suggesting we might want to think twice before putting a lot of weight on the latter. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩68b despite its profit of ₩19.7b, mentioned above. It's worth noting that KAON Group generated positive FCF of ₩41b a year ago, so at least they've done it in the past. Having said that, there is more to consider. We must also consider the impact of unusual items on statutory profit (and thus the accrual ratio), as well as note the ramifications of the company issuing new shares. One positive for KAON Group shareholders is that it's accrual ratio was significantly better last year, providing reason to believe that it may return to stronger cash conversion in the future. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

Check out our latest analysis for KAON Group

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of KAON Group.

One essential aspect of assessing earnings quality is to look at how much a company is diluting shareholders. As it happens, KAON Group issued 10% more new shares over the last year. As a result, its net income is now split between a greater number of shares. To talk about net income, without noticing earnings per share, is to be distracted by the big numbers while ignoring the smaller numbers that talk to per share value. You can see a chart of KAON Group's EPS by clicking here.

How Is Dilution Impacting KAON Group's Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

KAON Group was losing money three years ago. Zooming in to the last year, we still can't talk about growth rates coherently, since it made a loss last year. But mathematics aside, it is always good to see when a formerly unprofitable business come good (though we accept profit would have been higher if dilution had not been required). So you can see that the dilution has had a bit of an impact on shareholders.

In the long term, if KAON Group's earnings per share can increase, then the share price should too. But on the other hand, we'd be far less excited to learn profit (but not EPS) was improving. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

KAON Group's profit suffered from unusual items, which reduced profit by ₩4.0b in the last twelve months. In the case where this was a non-cash charge it would have made it easier to have high cash conversion, so it's surprising that the accrual ratio tells a different story. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And that's hardly a surprise given these line items are considered unusual. If KAON Group doesn't see those unusual expenses repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to increase over the coming year.

Our Take On KAON Group's Profit Performance

Summing up, KAON Group's unusual items suggest that its statutory earnings were temporarily depressed, and its accrual ratio indicates a lack of free cash flow relative to profit. On top of that, the dilution means that shareholders now own less of the company. Based on these factors, we think that KAON Group's statutory profits probably make it seem better than it is on an underlying level. data.title: What Investors Got Wrong About Iluka Resources Before The Drop
data.description:
Iluka Resources has been busy. The Eneabba rare earths refinery has secured a A$1.65b government loan and its first binding offtake with a global automaker, yet the share price moved the other way. For Iluka Resources shareholders, the loss over the past year was 23.0%, including dividends. If you had bought in a year ago on the rare earths story, how should this gap between ambitious projects and actual return be interpreted?

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Iluka Resources is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 32 best rare earth metal stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Stories Iluka Resources Investors Were Choosing Between

The shares cost A$6.65 at the start of the period, which meant anyone backing Iluka Resources had to pick a side on what came next.

The bullish narrative put Fair Value at A$8.47, or 27% above the start price, hinging on Eneabba and Balranald delivering 16.3% revenue growth and a 16.2% profit margin over three years.

The bearish view set Fair Value at A$5.3, or 20% below the start price, and assumed a 10.4% revenue growth rate with a 9.9x future P/E to reflect rising costs and reserve pressure.

What The Evidence Did To The Iluka Resources Argument

The Eneabba loan and first rare earth offtake supported the bullish Iluka Resources story that projects would secure long-term demand, but the later H1 2026 numbers pointed in a different direction. Revenue fell to A$455.9m and the group moved from a A$92m profit to a A$23.9m loss, with net margin shifting from 15.9% to a negative 5.2%. Overall, the evidence was mixed.

The tension here rested on one assumption. Investors were effectively betting that project progress would coincide with healthier earnings. Next time you assess a similar situation, track whether new contracts and funding move in step with revenue, absolute profit and net margin in the next set of reported results.

What Iluka Resources' Lower Price Now Asks You To Believe

Today Iluka Resources trades at A$5.42, with this Narrative’s Fair Value sitting above that level according to Robbo, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative. The focus is on Iluka’s mix of mineral sands earnings and its planned move into rare earth refining.

On that view, a buyer now would be assuming Iluka successfully brings Eneabba and Balranald into sustained operation while keeping zircon exposed cash flows and project debt manageable.

"Over the longer term, however, Iluka is a more compelling proposition. The company operates in strategically important minerals, benefits from meaningful government backing, and the national importance of the Eneabba refinery makes it likely that the project will be supported through to completion."
